title: Geometry oracle false-negative still triple-delivers narration on the retries-exhausted path (CAM-373 residue)
description:
MEASURED LIVE this session (CAM-372 cycle, on binary 0.223.0 which already carries the CAM-373 fix). The operator's pane received the line `[cam] merge-watch: PR #300 BEHIND, ran gh pr update-branch (attempt 1/2)` THREE times, identical. The event log carries exactly ONE corresponding event:

    {"kind":"push-undelivered","detail":{"paneId":"%0","retriesExhausted":3,"reason":"retries-exhausted"}}

All three sends really landed. The oracle judged each one undelivered and retried.

WHAT CAM-373 DID AND DID NOT FIX. CAM-373 made sendKeysVerified (src/tmux/dispatch.ts) send EXACTLY ONCE when the pre-send idle gate times out, emitting reason 'pane-not-idle' with retriesExhausted 1. That path is now provably correct: five 'pane-not-idle' events in this same log, every one retriesExhausted:1. But the fix was scoped to the case where the code KNOWS the geometry oracle's precondition (an idle pane) is violated and consults it anyway.

THE RESIDUE: when the pane IS detected idle, the precondition HOLDS, the oracle is consulted legitimately, and it STILL returns a false negative. The unconditional `for attempt <= maxAttempts` loop then runs to exhaustion and delivers the same narration up to 3 times. This is a different defect from CAM-373 (precondition violated) and from CAM-361 (the 30s blocking window, which is what made these three lines ARRIVE after the operator had already observed PR #300 MERGED: that is reordering, not duplication). All three now have distinct, separately-measured causes.

WHY IT MATTERS: duplicate narration is not cosmetic. The orchestrator narrates from these lines, and a triplicated merge-watch line reads as three separate BEHIND events / three update-branch attempts when exactly one occurred. That is actively misleading state for a human reading the pane, and it misled this session's narration until the event log was probed.

SUSPECTED DIRECTION (NOT verified, needs its own grounding pass before any spec): the cursor-geometry pair can read unchanged for a send that did land. This is the residue already documented honestly in the dispatch.ts module header: the prompt-row discriminator is consulted ONLY when the geometry pair reads unchanged, so a payload whose wrap row starts with '>' or U+276F can forge an empty-composer reading. A candidate fix is dedup-on-identical-payload within a short window, making a repeat send unrepresentable regardless of the oracle's verdict, which is robust against ANY future oracle false-negative. The alternative is hardening the oracle itself, which the CAM-359 / CAM-364 / CAM-373 sequence suggests is a losing game: three consecutive cycles have now narrowed this oracle without eliminating its false-negative class.

SIDECAR-EXECUTED: needs a coherence rebuild after merge.

REPRODUCIBLE EVIDENCE: grep -o '"kind":"push-undelivered"[^}]*}' .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl | tail -10

spec.scope: Modify the idle-path retry loop in sendKeysVerified (src/tmux/dispatch.ts) so the physical tmux 'send-keys' spawn happens at most once per call: retry attempts after the first re-sample and re-verify delivery but never re-send the payload. This makes a repeat physical send of an identical payload unrepresentable within one call (approach A, dedup scoped to the call), fixing the triple-delivery of a narration line under a geometry-oracle false-negative on a detected-idle pane. Keep the delivered-on-first-attempt fast path, the retries-exhausted push-undelivered event on final non-confirmation, and the pane-not-idle unverified path all unchanged in outcome. Update test/dispatch.test.ts to assert the single physical send under persistent false-negative.
acceptanceCriteria: Under a detected-idle pane where the geometry oracle never confirms delivery, sendKeysVerified physically invokes tmux 'send-keys' exactly once rather than maxAttempts times. [oracle: a unit harness importing sendKeysVerified injects a tmuxSpawnFn that counts spawns whose args include 'send-keys', a capturePaneFn returning an idle pane, a sampleGeometryFn returning geometry that reads changed on every sample so delivery is never confirmed, maxAttempts 3, and a no-op sleepFn; the recorded send-keys count is 1. On unmodified main the same harness records 3.]

When the geometry oracle confirms delivery on the first attempt, sendKeysVerified still physically sends exactly once and emits no push-undelivered event. [oracle: the same harness with a sampleGeometryFn returning constant geometry and a visibleCaptureFn returning a cursor row that starts with a prompt glyph records a send-keys count of 1 and zero logged events.]

The pane-not-idle path stays unchanged: when the pane never reads idle, sendKeysVerified sends exactly once via the unverified path and emits one push-undelivered event whose reason is 'pane-not-idle' and whose retriesExhausted is 1. [oracle: the harness with a capturePaneFn returning a busy pane and idleTimeoutMs 1 records a send-keys count of 1 and exactly one push-undelivered event with reason equal to 'pane-not-idle' and retriesExhausted equal to 1.]
gotchas: The triple-delivery is intra-call: one sendKeysVerified invocation, and the for-attempt loop physically sends on every iteration at the send-keys spawn line. A per-call send-once guard, not a cross-call wall-clock window, is the correct scope, because distinct narration lines are always distinct calls, so a per-call guard cannot suppress a legitimately repeated line.

Do not introduce module-level mutable state such as a Map keyed by paneId: grounding showed the file has no module-level mutable state today, and a process-lived Map would leak between test cases and reintroduce the legitimate-repeat suppression risk. Keep the guard as a local flag inside the call.
The retries-exhausted event field retriesExhausted stays at maxAttempts and now counts verify attempts, not physical sends; do not change its value.
src/tmux/dispatch.ts is sidecar-executed because the sidecar pushes narration through sendKeysVerified, so a coherence rebuild is mandatory after merge.
Keep the settle sleep and the inter-attempt backoff in place so a genuinely slow pane still gets time to register delivery before the next verify.
domainTerms: sendKeysVerified: the dispatch function that pushes a narration line to a tmux pane and verifies delivery via the geometry oracle.
geometry oracle: the geometryUnchanged plus cursorRowStartsWithPrompt pair that judges whether a send landed; the module header documents that it can false-negative on a detected-idle pane.
retries-exhausted: the push-undelivered reason emitted when the verify loop finishes without confirming delivery.
